days.note: Big mid-period S swell (7ft @ 11s, ~1189 kJ) easing, light winds and fair-good at dawn. Manly (North Steyne) cleanest, chest–head; Dee Why wrap is poor (176°). Get in before 9am, S/SE bump after.
days.surfline_text: Raw size and energy will have calmed down compared to Friday as mid-period S swell eases through the day and we see a little E swell. Head to OH at S magnets - with more OH sets in the morning. Sheltered S corners about waist high. Chest to head for other breaks.  It's gone offshore W to SW winds at dawn - should last until about 9am. Best to get on it asap.  Then light to moderate S/SE'lies add some bump / wobble but it should be alrightish.

days.surfline_text: We're looking to see the S swell drift further SSE and ease with some building E swell - head high or so for S exposures, about waist to chest elsewhere.  It'll be hard to find anything clean though with persistent easterly winds adding plenty of lump and wobble to the surf.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Sat junky: short-period SSE + E windswell, onshore. Sun the better of the two: SE/E mix, head high at S exposures, light wind at dawn only. Sun dawn is the window.
days.surfline_text: Short period SSE swell is joined by some easterly windswells. Sth magnets will still be picking up the most size - in the head high plus range. Most other beaches will be waist to chest.  We're still going to be battling the onshore winds - best chance for something more appealing will be in the early morning and maybe at the very S facing breaks if we get a bit of N in the wind. I think it will be pretty junky though. SE and E swell mix should give us something head high at the south exposures with waist to chest at other breaks.  Hopefully winds play ball for the early and we see clean surf at the south exposures, elsewhere likely more wobbly / lumpy. Then probably going onshore and lumpy from mid-morning.
